title: Knee Jerk and Gut Reactions: When We Are Not in Control
titleZh: 膝跳反应与本能反应：当我们失去控制时
credits: Anna Matteo wrote this story for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: And now, Words and Their Stories, from VOA Learning English.
sentences.zh: 现在是“词汇与故事”，来自美国之音英语学习。

sentences.en: In life, some of our decisions and actions are well thought out.
sentences.zh: 在生活中，我们的一些决定和行动是经过深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: They involve research, examination, and time for thought.
sentences.zh: 它们涉及研究、审查和思考的时间。

sentences.en: And other decisions and actions are not well thought out.
sentences.zh: 而其他一些决定和行动则不是经过深思熟虑的。

sentences.en: We make them quickly, without thinking, almost like a pure physical reaction.
sentences.zh: 我们很快地做出这些决定，不加思考，几乎就像一种纯粹的生理反应。

sentences.en: We can call these decisions, actions or reactions knee-jerk.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把这些决定、行动或反应称为“膝跳反应”。

sentences.en: This term comes from a medical process.
sentences.zh: 这个术语来自一种医疗过程。

sentences.en: Meriam Webster defines the noun "knee jerk" as “an involuntary forward kick produced by a light blow on the tendon below the kneecap.”
sentences.zh: 《韦氏词典》把名词“knee jerk”定义为“对膝盖骨下方肌腱轻轻一击所产生的不受控制的向前踢的动作”。

sentences.en: It is an involuntary action. It's automatic.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不受控制的反应，它是自动发生的。

sentences.en: The words “involuntary” and “automatic” are important when understanding the term “knee jerk” and when to use it.
sentences.zh: 在理解“膝跳反应”这一术语以及何时使用它时，“不受控制的”和“自动的”这两个词很重要。

sentences.en: Knee-jerk reactions seem to happen automatically without a decision-making process.
sentences.zh: 膝跳反应似乎是在没有决策过程的情况下自动发生的。

sentences.en: We often use “knee jerk” as an adjective.
sentences.zh: 我们经常把“knee jerk”用作形容词。

sentences.en: Like hitting your kneecap to move your leg, knee-jerk reactions or statements also seem like an involuntary reflex.
sentences.zh: 就像敲击膝盖骨来移动你的腿一样，膝跳反应或言论似乎也是一种不受控制的反射。

sentences.en: "Knee jerk" also describes predictable behavior.
sentences.zh: “knee jerk”也用来描述可预测的行为。

sentences.en: Again, hit the knee, the leg will kick every time.
sentences.zh: 同样，敲击膝盖，腿每次都踢。

sentences.en: So "knee jerk" describes someone who always reacts quickly and without enough thought.
sentences.zh: 所以“knee jerk”用来描述那些总是迅速反应而思考不足的人。

sentences.en: For example, let’s say you are on a team with someone who never faces responsibility for their mistakes in the game.
sentences.zh: 例如，假设你和一个人同在一个队里，而这个人从不为自己在比赛中的错误承担责任。

sentences.en: If brought to account, the player always blames the dropped ball on other teammates.
sentences.zh: 如果被追究责任，这位球员总是把掉球的责任推给其他队友。

sentences.en: You can say that player is having a knee-jerk reaction to criticism.
sentences.zh: 你可以说这位球员对批评做出了膝跳反应。

sentences.en: They have a go-to response.
sentences.zh: 他们有一套惯用的回应。

sentences.en: It’s like a reflex they can’t control.
sentences.zh: 这就像一种他们无法控制的反射。

sentences.en: We often use knee-jerk in a criticizing or negative way.
sentences.zh: 我们经常以批评或否定的方式使用"knee-jerk"（膝跳反射/本能的）。

sentences.en: Now, a gut reaction also happens without thinking.
sentences.zh: 现在，"gut reaction"（直觉反应）也是在不经思考的情况下发生的。

sentences.en: But it is a bit different than a knee-jerk response.
sentences.zh: 但它与"knee-jerk response"（本能反应）略有不同。

sentences.en: A gut reaction is a feeling.
sentences.zh: "gut reaction"是一种感觉。

sentences.en: When we have a gut reaction, our instincts are telling us that something may not be right.
sentences.zh: 当我们产生直觉反应时，我们的本能告诉我们某事可能不对劲。

sentences.en: Gut reactions are instinctual warnings.
sentences.zh: 直觉反应是本能的警告。

sentences.en: So, we also use this expression a bit differently than "knee jerk."
sentences.zh: 因此，我们使用这个表达的方式也与"knee jerk"略有不同。

sentences.en: We usually talk about our own gut reactions or impulses, not others.
sentences.zh: 我们通常谈论的是自己的直觉反应或冲动，而不是别人的。

sentences.en: Here is an example:
sentences.zh: 下面是一个例子：

sentences.en: One day, I was hiking on a mountain in California.
sentences.zh: 有一天，我在加利福尼亚的一座山上徒步。

sentences.en: I had hiked for about two hours and was near the top.
sentences.zh: 我已经徒步了大约两个小时，快到达山顶了。

sentences.en: The view, I was told, was truly beautiful.
sentences.zh: 据说那里的景色非常美丽。

sentences.en: I couldn’t wait to see it!
sentences.zh: 我迫不及待地想看看！

sentences.en: Then, suddenly, I had a strange feeling.
sentences.zh: 然后，突然地，我有一种奇怪的感觉。

sentences.en: Something just didn’t feel right.
sentences.zh: 某件事就是让我觉得不对劲。

sentences.en: I can’t explain why, but my gut instinct was to turn around and head back down the mountain.
sentences.zh: 我无法解释原因，但我的本能告诉我应该转身下山。

sentences.en: I later found out that a dangerous bear had been sighted in the same area that I had fled.
sentences.zh: 后来我得知，在我逃离的同一区域曾发现过一只危险的熊。

sentences.en: I am so thankful I listened to my gut instinct.
sentences.zh: 我很感激我听从了自己的本能。

sentences.en: And that’s Words and Their Stories.
sentences.zh: 以上就是"Words and Their Stories"（词语及其故事）。

sentences.en: Until next time, I’m Anna Matteo.
sentences.zh: 我们下次见，我是安娜·马特奥。

glossary.def: not normally under the control of the will
glossary.zh: 非自愿的；不受意志控制的

glossary.def: largely or wholly involuntary :acting or done without conscious thought or intention
an automatic response to a stimulus in which a nerve message passes from a sense organ to the spinal cord and then to a point of action (as a muscle or gland) often without first passing to the brain
glossary.zh: 反射；对刺激的自动反应

glossary.def: behavior that is based on automatic actions
glossary.zh: 本能；基于自动行为的行为
